_comment_1: ATOMIC GRANULARITY ONLY. One row per requirement, not per chapter. A 14-day project should produce on the order of 100 rows. If your row count is implausibly low for project age, the loop will self-terminate before the product is good. This is the Flatline failure mode.
_comment_2: Allowed status values: not_started | partial | done | deprecated. Every row should carry implementationRefs and testRefs once status >= partial. followupRefs link to F-NNN entries in FOLLOWUPS.md. A row marked status=deprecated stays in the ledger for institutional memory but no implementation or tests are owed; add a note in the row explaining what removed it from scope (slice id, Q-NNN resolution, etc.).

rows.requirement: Timeline persistence: actions performed during a time period are recorded and replay as a permanent past instance whenever another instance witnesses that period from outside it.
rows.note: Per-tick input recording buffer captures keyboard state plus normalized time-of-day each fixed step. A ghost capsule (`createGhost`) drains a frozen recording back into a separate Rapier dynamic capsule body tick-for-tick, integrated through the same fixed-step physics loop as the active player. `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) snapshots the active player's lifetime recording onto a ghost on every lit-portal entry and resets the recorder to a fresh buffer keyed at tick 0 of the destination timeline. Per-timeline ghost bookkeeping lands in `src/sim/timelineRegistry.ts`: ghosts are filed against the timeline they were RECORDED IN (the SOURCE timeline at traversal, derived from `lifetime.originNormalized`). The registry's `activeGhosts()` returns only the ghosts in the timeline the active player is currently inside, and the host's loop iterates that list rather than every spawned ghost, so an action recorded in timeline T replays only when another instance witnesses T from outside it (re-enters T). On `setActiveTimeline(next)` every ghost in the entering bucket is reset to its tick-0 spawn pose with zero velocity and made visible; ghosts in the leaving bucket are hidden. Each timeline visit is a fresh playback (the cleaner mental model: a timeline records WHAT happened, and re-entering replays it from the start).

rows.requirement: Past instances replay recorded input frame-exact and cannot be altered, only worked around or physically redirected.
rows.note: End-to-end ghost replay landed: `createGhost` builds a Three.js mesh + Rapier dynamic capsule whose `advanceTick()` writes `replayAtTick(recording, tickIndex)` onto the body's planar velocity each fixed step, preserving y so gravity is not overwritten. The recording itself is deeply frozen at snapshot time so it cannot be mutated after capture. Past the end of the recording the ghost writes a zero planar velocity each tick and decelerates to a stop under the same linear damping as the active player. The ghost is a dynamic body with the same capsule collider as the player so it can be physically redirected (worked around) but not altered. `applyInstanceTint` stamps each ghost with its origin-time color so the player can read which timeline a ghost came from.

rows.requirement: Traveling through a portal does not erase the prior timeline; the entered instance continues to exist as a recorded instance in the timeline left behind.
rows.note: `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) snapshots the active player's lifetime recording on every lit-portal entry and spawns a ghost replaying the snapshot from the lifetime's start position. `TimelineRegistry` (`src/sim/timelineRegistry.ts`) files the spawned ghost into the SOURCE timeline (the timeline being LEFT BEHIND, derived from `lifetime.originNormalized` via `timelineIdFromNormalized`) so the recording is keyed against the timeline it captured, not the destination. After traversal the registry's active timeline switches to the destination; the source timeline's ghost is hidden and stilled but persists in its bucket. When the active player returns to the source timeline (e.g. East from 5:00 to 6:00 then West back to 5:00 in the GDD's Act 2 first loop), `setActiveTimeline` resets every ghost in the entering bucket to its tick-0 spawn pose and makes it visible, so the recorded instance replays the path the active player walked when it was the active instance in that timeline. The recording is preserved as a permanent past instance in the timeline being left behind.

rows.requirement: System enforces the no-paradox invariant: a player cannot prevent themselves from having done something they already did.
rows.note: No-paradox invariants codified as property-style tests. `tests/sim/noParadox.test.ts` (6 cases, each running 100 randomized input sequences derived from a hand-rolled 32-bit Lehmer LCG seeded from the test name per Q-017 default) pins the four invariants from `docs/gdd/40-act-progress-and-narrative-beats.md` section 7. Invariant 1 (recording immutability post-snapshot): the snapshot's outer object, frames array, and per-frame keys are all `Object.isFrozen` true; further recording past the snapshot point does not perturb the snapshot's observable state; explicit mutation attempts (push to `frames`, write to `frame.tick`, write to `frame.keys`, overwrite `length`) are silently rejected or throw under strict mode and leave the snapshot observably unchanged. Invariant 2 (registry monotonicity): a 50-op random sequence mixing 70% `add` and 30% `setActiveTimeline` against `createTimelineRegistry({ initialTimeline: 5 })` keeps the total ghost count across timelines {5, 6, 12} monotonically non-decreasing; `clearAllGhosts` is the only operation that returns the count to zero. Invariant 3 (tick-K causality): a ghost built from a recording snapshot at tick K produces bit-identical body translations across 20 fixed simulation steps regardless of whether the source recorder kept recording past K, and `replayAtTick(snap, t)` reads the same value before and after the recorder is mutated past K. Invariant 4 (cross-cutting key stability): a snapshot's per-frame keys are equality-stable after the recording is filed into a registry and the ghost runs five fixed simulation steps. NO production code change; the existing `InputRecorder` / `TimelineRegistry` / `GhostInstance` / `replayAtTick` implementations already satisfy every invariant.

rows.requirement: Portals have fixed locations and fixed destinations; a given door always leads to the same other time.
rows.note: Portal data model lands in `src/sim/portal.ts`. `createPortal({ door, destinationHours, isLit })` returns a frozen object with `readonly destinationHours` so the destination cannot mutate at runtime. Validation rejects non-finite destinations and destinations outside `[0, 24)` so callers downstream can trust the range. `createActOnePortals(doors)` produces the canonical four-door Act 1 configuration (South lit -> 12:00, East lit -> 6:00, North dark, West dark) and `src/scene/room.ts` consumes it at room build time. The runtime traversal half (REQ-009 send-the-player) shipped in PR #15. Polish flip: `tests/sim/portal.test.ts > REQ-005 portal destination fixity property test` runs a 1000-tick fuzz that picks a random portal each tick (via a hand-rolled LCG seeded from the test name per Q-017 default) and attempts to assign new values to `destinationHours`, `direction`, and `isLit`; `Object.freeze` rejects every write under strict mode and the per-tick assertions confirm all four portals' fixed fields are unchanged from their construction-time snapshot.

rows.requirement: An unvisited future contains no recorded events and no instances; a time period only contains events once an instance has entered it.
rows.note: `TimelineRegistry.ghostsFor(timeline)` returns an empty list for any timeline that no portal traversal has filed a ghost into, and `activeGhosts()` (driven by the host's per-fixed-step loop) returns an empty list when the active timeline is unvisited. Combined with `wireTraversal` only filing ghosts into the SOURCE timeline of a lit-portal entry, this enforces the GDD's 'an unvisited future contains nothing' invariant for ghost playback: walking East from 5:00 into 6:00 for the first time arrives at an empty 6:00, because no instance has ever recorded a path there. The end-to-end invariant is now provably tested across timelines: `tests/sim/portalTraversal.test.ts > first entry into 6:00 yields an empty active-ghost list` asserts that after East-from-5:00 entry the registry's `activeGhosts()` is `[]` while the 5:00 bucket holds the spawned recording. Lit/dark state derivation (REQ-011) is the remaining cross-cutting recorded-event class; that row tracks the rest of REQ-011's scope and the registry already exposes the per-timeline ghost counts REQ-011 will consume.

rows.requirement: Instance generation numbering tracks generations from the original spawn (You1, You-1, You-2, ...).
rows.note: `src/sim/instanceId.ts` exports the `InstanceId` type (positive monotonic integer; 1 = You1, 2 = You-1, 3 = You-2), `INITIAL_INSTANCE_ID = 1`, `formatInstanceId(id)` (the GDD-canonical display label: `formatInstanceId(1) === 'You1'`, `formatInstanceId(n)` for n > 1 is `'You-' + (n - 1)`), and `nextInstanceId(id)` (returns `id + 1`). The id is threaded through the active player handle (`Player.instanceId` seeded by `createPlayer` at `INITIAL_INSTANCE_ID`), the active lifetime (`ActiveLifetime.instanceId`), the active player handle for traversal (`ActivePlayerHandle.instanceId`), and ghost instances (`GhostInstance.instanceId`, `CreateGhostOptions.instanceId`). On every lit-portal traversal `wireTraversal` hands the OUTGOING active player's `instanceId` (via `lifetime.instanceId`) to the spawned ghost (the ghost IS that closed-out instance, replayed) and advances the active player to `nextInstanceId(previous)` (REQ-008). `hardReset` returns both `player.instanceId` and `lifetime.instanceId` to `INITIAL_INSTANCE_ID` so the next spawn is again You1. UI rendering of the label is OUT of scope this slice; the data feeds the future REQ-032 thought-bubble overlay.

rows.requirement: Player input always controls the most recently spawned active instance.
rows.note: Encoded in the lit-portal traversal handoff. On every lit entry `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) takes the OUTGOING active player's `instanceId` and hands it to the spawned ghost (which IS that closed-out instance, replayed), then advances the active player's `instanceId` to `nextInstanceId(previous)` and writes the same id onto the freshly-opened lifetime. The active player therefore always carries the most recently spawned generation: a sequence of N traversals leaves the active player at instance N+1 with N closed-out ghosts in their respective source timelines, each ghost retaining its own instanceId across timeline switches. `tests/sim/portalTraversal.test.ts > instance generation numbering` covers the chain end-to-end (1 -> 2 -> 3) including the cross-timeline retention case. The keyboard input layer continues to write through the single `player` handle the host wires into `wireTraversal`, so player input is by construction always routed to the most recently spawned active instance.

rows.requirement: A lit door is enterable and sends the player to the door's fixed destination time.
rows.note: End-to-end traversal lands in `src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`. `wireTraversal` subscribes to the `PortalTriggerSet` from PR #14, filters `enter` events on `isLit(portal)`, and on each lit entry: snapshots the active player's lifetime recorder onto a ghost spawned at the lifetime's start position with the lifetime's `originNormalized` as the tint (so the ghost belongs to the timeline being LEFT BEHIND), teleports the active player to the destination spawn pose (room center default; pluggable via `resolveSpawnPose` for per-time spawn poses in the next slice), zeros the player's velocity, re-stamps `player.originNormalized` and the player mesh tint via `applyInstanceTint(destinationNormalized)` (REQ-030), and opens a fresh `InputRecorder` keyed at tick 0 of the destination timeline. Dark portals are filtered (REQ-010). `src/app.ts` constructs an `ActiveLifetime` next to the player and wires the traversal handler; the per-fixed-step recording call resolves against the lifetime's current recorder so a swap on traversal does not require re-binding. The destination spawn pose detail (per-time spawn poses authored from the GDD's Act 1 anchors at 5:00 and 6:00) lands as REQ-013/REQ-014 in the next slice; the resolver hook is in place for that slice to drop in a real lookup.

rows.requirement: A dark door is a spawn-only exit; instances emerge from it and the player cannot enter.
rows.note: Dark portal half of the data model lands in `src/sim/portal.ts`. The Act 1 canonical table marks North and West dark per the GDD; `applyDoorLitState(door, false)` stamps the dark visual (near-black diffuse, no emissive). `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) filters `enter` events on `isLit(portal)`, so dark portals do NOT teleport the player or spawn a ghost; this enforces the 'player cannot enter' half of REQ-010. The spawn-only-emergence runtime half (instances emerging through dark doors when arriving from a recorded timeline) is naturally satisfied by the per-timeline ghost bookkeeping in `src/sim/timelineRegistry.ts`: a ghost recorded entering through a lit portal in its source timeline is filed against that source timeline and replays from its tick-0 spawn pose on re-entry, which is the dark-side emergence semantic the GDD describes. Polish flip: `tests/sim/portalTraversal.test.ts > REQ-010 regression: walking into the West dark portal at 5:00 leaves the player capsule's translation unchanged` simulates the canonical case from `ACT_ONE_PORTAL_SPECS` (West dark at 5:00) by placing the player inside the West trigger volume and firing a `step` event, then asserting the player's body translation is unchanged, the active timeline is still 5, and no ghost was spawned.

rows.requirement: Door lit-versus-dark state is computed from arriving instances in the recorded timeline, not stored as a discoverable variable.
rows.note: Lit/dark state is now computed by `litStateForTimeline(timeline, { ghosts, blockedByArrivals? })` in `src/sim/litStateForTimeline.ts` as `seed[timeline][cardinal] && !blockedByArrivals(ghosts, cardinal)`. The seed is the canonical Acts 1-3 starting state from `DOOR_STATE_BY_HOUR` (5:00 South+East lit, 6:00 West-only-lit, every other cardinal dark). The arrivals predicate `BlockedByArrivals` is the data path future Acts 2-3 narrative beats will populate; the MVP body `DEFAULT_BLOCKED_BY_ARRIVALS` returns `false` for every input because Acts 1-3 starting state does not yet have a beat that blocks a door via arrivals (the seeded state already encodes the GDD's intent). For unauthored hours the function returns `null` and `wireTraversal` falls back to the portal's frozen `isLit` flag (preserving pre-REQ-011 behavior for test fixtures that exercise unauthored hours). `src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`'s `isLitForCurrentTimeline` reads through `litStateForTimeline(registry.activeTimeline, { ghosts: registry.ghostsFor(registry.activeTimeline) })` so the registry's per-timeline ghost list flows into the predicate's input. The visual paint path (`repaintDoorsForHour`, `room.ts`) still calls `doorLitStateAtHour` directly because the arrivals stub returns `false` (paint matches gate); F-006 unifies both call sites once Acts 2-3 introduce a non-trivial arrivals rule.

rows.requirement: Act 1 cinematic at 12:00: two figures drag a knocked-out body through the North door to the center of the room, then fade to black.
rows.note: Act 1 cinematic data path lands via scripted actor recordings reusing the existing `GhostInstance` / `TimelineRegistry` pipeline (per `docs/gdd/40-act-progress-and-narrative-beats.md` section 5). New module `src/sim/scripts/act1Cinematic.ts` exports three frozen `InputRecording` objects (`ACT1_LEFT_DRAGGER_RECORDING`, `ACT1_RIGHT_DRAGGER_RECORDING`, `ACT1_KNOCKOUT_BODY_RECORDING`), three spawn poses (`ACT1_LEFT_DRAGGER_SPAWN = { x: -0.6, z: -3.5 }`, `ACT1_RIGHT_DRAGGER_SPAWN = { x: 0.6, z: -3.5 }`, `ACT1_KNOCKOUT_BODY_SPAWN = { x: 0, z: -3.6 }`), the timing constants (`ACT1_CINEMATIC_DURATION_TICKS = 240`, `ACT1_CINEMATIC_FADE_START_TICK = 180`, `ACT1_CINEMATIC_FADE_DURATION_TICKS = 60`, `ACT1_DRAGGER_WALK_TICKS = 60`), and the host hook `mountAct1Cinematic({ registry, scene, world })` which builds three `GhostInstance` objects via `createGhost` (instance ids 101, 102, 103) and files them into the 12:00 bucket via `registry.add(12, ghost)`. Dragger recordings hold `back: true, pickup: true` for the first 60 ticks then idle for 180 ticks; the body recording is a single all-zero frame (Q-021 default A) with the ghost flipped to `unconscious` post-creation via `applyKnockout`. New module `src/render/fadeOverlay.ts` exports `createFadeOverlay({ colorHex? })` which builds a Three.js full-screen plane on a separate orthographic camera with `setOpacity(t)` (clamped to `[0, 1]`, hides at zero), `render(renderer)` (composites over the main pass with `autoClear = false`), and `dispose()`. `src/app.ts` mounts the cinematic at boot (active timeline at boot is 5:00 so the cinematic ghosts open hidden via the registry's `add` non-active-bucket hide path) and constructs the fade overlay; the overlay's `render` runs after the main `renderer.render` each frame. Q-012 / Q-013 / Q-015 / Q-016 / Q-021 defaults are consumed. The visible body-tracking-the-actors behavior is OUT of scope this slice (the host's carry resolver only fires for the active player); the data path and the predicate gate (`isAct1Spawn` reads `ghostsFor(12).length >= 3 && currentTimeline === 5`) ship clean.

rows.requirement: Act 1 spawn at 5:00: the player stands in the center of the room, with North and West dark and South and East lit.
rows.note: Act 1 spawn pose lands end-to-end. `src/sim/actOneAnchor.ts` defines `ACT_ONE_HOUR = 5`, `ACT_ONE_NORMALIZED = 5 / 24`, and `hourToNormalized(hours)` as the canonical 24-hour day-arc convention. `src/app.ts` constructs `TimeOfDay` with `initialNormalized: ACT_ONE_NORMALIZED` so the opening frame reads the 5:00 amber background tint and the player capsule's `originNormalized` stamps to 5/24 (REQ-030). The player still spawns at the room center per PR #4. `src/sim/doorStateAtTime.ts` (`doorLitStateAtHour(5)`) is the canonical lit/dark table for the 5:00 timeline (South lit, East lit, North dark, West dark) and `src/scene/room.ts` now reads through the helper at room-build time so the four-door visual state at the opening frame matches the GDD spec.

rows.requirement: Door destinations from 5:00: South leads to 12:00 and East leads to 6:00.
rows.note: Door destinations from 5:00 are wired end-to-end. `ACT_ONE_PORTAL_SPECS` (PR #12) authors South to 12:00 and East to 6:00; `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) reads `portal.destinationHours` via `portalDestinationNormalized` to drive both the player teleport's destination resolver and the re-stamped `originNormalized` tint. With this slice's 5:00 clock anchor (`ACT_ONE_NORMALIZED` from `src/sim/actOneAnchor.ts`) the player physically opens at 5:00 with the matching 5:00 amber background, so entering the South door sends the player to 12:00 and entering the East door sends the player to 6:00 from the canonical opening state. The 6:00-side door state (REQ-015 'West-only lit') is forward-authored in `DOOR_STATE_BY_HOUR[6]` so the next slice can drop in cleanly.

rows.requirement: 6:00 timeline state: the room is empty, only the West door is lit, and the West door leads back to 5:00.
rows.note: Traversing East from 5:00 now drops the player into a properly empty 6:00 room with West-only lit and the West door routing back to 5:00. `src/sim/timelineRoom.ts` exposes `repaintDoorsForHour(portals, hour)` (stamps each portal door's lit/dark visual via `applyDoorLitState(portal.door, doorLitStateAtHour(hour)[portal.direction])`) and `snapClockToHour(timeOfDay, hour)` (sets the time-of-day clock so the room background tints at the destination hour). `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) gains an `onTimelineEnter(destinationHour)` callback fired AFTER the registry's active timeline switches; `src/app.ts` wires the callback to call both helpers on every lit traversal. The traversal handler's lit/dark gate now reads `DOOR_STATE_BY_HOUR[registry.activeTimeline][portal.direction]` for authored hours and falls back to `portal.isLit` for unauthored hours, so the West portal (authored DARK at 5:00 in `ACT_ONE_PORTAL_SPECS`) is ENTERABLE at 6:00 per the table without any portal-data rewrite. The 6:00-side door state was forward-authored in `DOOR_STATE_BY_HOUR[6]` by PR #16 (West lit, others dark) and the West portal's `destinationHours = 5` was already authored in PR #12, so no portal data change was needed. First entry into 6:00 yields an empty active-ghost list (REQ-006: an unvisited future contains nothing) and the West door at 6:00 routes back to 5:00.

rows.requirement: Act 2 first loop: traveling East then West produces a You-1 instance who replays You1's path, walks West, and disappears.
rows.note: Integration test in `tests/sim/act2Loop1.test.ts` drives the existing primitives (recorder, traversal, registry, ghost) through the GDD's scripted Act 2 first-loop sequence: at 5:00 the active player records an East-bound walk and crosses the East trigger; the lit-portal traversal handler files the You1 ghost into bucket 5 and switches the active timeline to 6. At 6:00 the player records a West-bound walk and crosses the West trigger; the traversal handler files the You-1 ghost into bucket 6 and switches the active timeline back to 5, which resets the original 5:00-recorded ghost to its tick-0 spawn pose and makes it visible. Driving `advanceTick` for the recording's full length brings the ghost's tick index up to its recording length, satisfying `allGhostsAtRest` in the `isAct2Loop1` predicate. The test then projects the live registry plus the active player into an `ActStateSnapshot` (the same projection the host loop will perform once REQ-016+ slices wire the observer into `src/app.ts`) and asserts `ActStateObserver.update(snapshot)` walks the chain through `act-1-spawn` (cinematic in 12:00 from `mountAct1Cinematic` at boot) and lands at `act-2-loop-1`. A second case asserts ghost-A's per-tick replay velocity is byte-identical to the recording's `inputToVelocity(keys)` for every tick, pinning the determinism guarantee that backs the GDD's 'and disappears' semantics. NO production code touched; the existing `isAct2Loop1` predicate from PR #30 fires correctly on the snapshot the live state produces.

rows.requirement: Act 2 second loop: knocking out You-1 on return to 5:00 and dragging the body East to 6:00 produces a You-2 instance who wakes and knocks out You1.
rows.note: Integration test in `tests/sim/act2Loop2.test.ts` drives the existing primitives (recorder, traversal, registry, ghost, knockout, carry) through the GDD's scripted Act 2 second-loop sequence. Phase 1+2 reuses the loop-1 sequence (a helper `runLoopOne` walks East 5 to 6 then West 6 to 5, leaving ghost-A in bucket 5 and ghost-B in bucket 6, active timeline 5, ghost-A replayed to exhaustion). Phase 3a positions the active player adjacent to ghost-A and applies the same side effects the host's punch resolver does (`applyKnockout` flips ghost-A to unconscious; `applyKnockoutBodyResponse` writes the impulse plus mesh tilt). Phase 3b drives `resolveCarryToggle` on a one-tick rising edge and asserts the resulting state is `{ kind: 'carrying', carriedId: ghostA.instanceId }`; `applyCarryPickup` flips ghost-A's body to KinematicPositionBased. Phase 3c records four input frames (right + pickup) and runs `applyCarryAttachment` per tick; `detector.step` then crosses the East trigger at 5:00 (East lit per `DOOR_STATE_BY_HOUR`), and the lit-portal traversal handler files the carrying-East lifetime as a fresh ghost in bucket 5 (so bucket 5 ends with at least 2 ghosts: the original unconscious ghost-A plus the dragging-East ghost-C), switches active timeline to 6, and the carry state passes through unchanged (`wireTraversal` does not branch on `player.carry`). Phase 3d asserts post-traversal: active=6, player.carry preserved, bucket 5 has an unconscious ghost (ghost-A retained its flag because `setActiveTimeline` only HIDES the leaving bucket; reset only fires on entering-bucket re-entry), bucket 6 still holds ghost-B. Phase 4 resolves the GDD's 'wait for another instance to wake up' beat per Q-023 default A: the test directly applies `applyKnockout(player.consciousness)` plus `applyKnockoutBodyResponse(player.body, player.mesh, ...)`, modelling the outcome of a recorded punch tick from a future loop iteration (the GDD's load-bearing state change is You1 going down at 6:00; the wake mechanic is narrative dressing under v1's permanent-unconsciousness rule). Phase 5 builds the snapshot and asserts `isAct2Loop2` returns true plus the observer (already advanced to `act-2-loop-1` mid-test via an explicit update at the end of Phase 1+2) walks to `act-2-loop-2`. A second case pins the four conjunctions of `isAct2Loop2` (currentTimeline === 6, activePlayer.consciousness === 'unconscious', ghosts5 has at least one unconscious, ghosts6 non-empty) by satisfying the full state then dropping each conjunction in turn and asserting `isAct2Loop2` returns false. NO production code touched: the existing `isAct2Loop2` predicate from PR #30 fires correctly on the live-state snapshot.

rows.requirement: Act 3 setup: repeating the Act 2 sequence positions a knocked-out instance at 6:00 and the player waits for the other instance to wake.
rows.note: Integration test in `tests/sim/act3Setup.test.ts` drives the existing primitives (recorder, traversal, registry, ghost, knockout, carry, instanceId) through the GDD's scripted Act 3 setup beat. Phase 1 reuses the Loop 1 plus Loop 2 sequence (helpers `runLoopOne` and `runLoopTwo`) to land at active=6 with the active player unconscious at 6:00, bucket 5 holding the unconscious ghost-A plus the dragging-East ghost-C, bucket 6 holding the loop-1 West-bound ghost-B. The observer is opened mid-test and fed the loop-1 then loop-2 snapshots so the watermark advances to `act-2-loop-2`. Phase 2 begins the Act 3 fresh lifetime at 5:00 via a new `beginNewLifetimeAt5` helper that mirrors the lifetime-rollover the host's traversal handler runs on a lit-portal traversal (`wireTraversal` step 1-7), minus the trigger event: it files the prior unconscious lifetime as a ghost in bucket 6 (using the recorder's snapshot, post-flipped to unconscious via `applyKnockout` in the same pattern `mountAct1Cinematic` uses for the Act 1 body ghost), advances the active player's `instanceId` via `nextInstanceId`, opens a fresh `InputRecorder`, restamps `originNormalized` to 5/24, places the body at the room center, clears velocity / rotation / mesh tilt, and finally calls `setActiveTimeline(5)` (which hides bucket 6 leaving the unconscious ghost unconscious because hide does NOT reset, and resets bucket 5 ghosts to tick 0 conscious per REQ-033 reset semantics; the act-3-setup predicate does not read bucket 5 so the conscious reset is harmless). To make the recorder snapshot non-empty at the boundary, `runLoopTwo` records one idle frame at 6:00 BEFORE the knockout (the East traversal swapped to a fresh recorder; without the idle frame the recorder would be empty and the prior lifetime would silently skip the file step). Phase 3 builds the snapshot and asserts `isAct3Setup(snapshot) === true` plus `observer.update(snapshot)` walks from `act-2-loop-2` to `act-3-setup`. A second case pins the two conjunctions of `isAct3Setup` (currentTimeline === 5, ghosts6.some(unconscious)) by satisfying the full state, then dropping each conjunction in turn (currentTimeline switched to 6, no unconscious ghost in bucket 6 by mapping the projection to conscious) and asserting `isAct3Setup` returns false on each variant. NO production code touched: the existing `isAct3Setup` predicate from PR #30 fires correctly on the live-state snapshot once the lifetime-boundary mechanism is exercised; the predicate's `currentTimeline === 5 && ghostsFor(6).some(g => g.consciousness === 'unconscious')` is the correct dossier-pseudocode mapping for the Act 3 setup beat (the watermark prerequisite is enforced by the observer's monotonic walk, not by the predicate).

rows.requirement: Act 3 chase beat: running toward the West door while another instance chases pulls both instances through to 5:00 in the same frame.
rows.note: Integration test in `tests/sim/act3Chase.test.ts` drives the dossier-prescribed Act 3 chase: Phase 1 reuses the loop-1 plus loop-2 helpers (`runLoopOne`, `runLoopTwo`) to land at active=6 with the player unconscious at 6:00. Phase 2's `beginNewLifetimeAt5` files the prior unconscious lifetime as a ghost in bucket 6 and opens a fresh conscious lifetime at 5:00, transitioning the observer from `act-2-loop-2` to `act-3-setup`. Phase 3 walks East to traverse to 6:00 (East lit at 5:00 per `DOOR_STATE_BY_HOUR`). Phase 4 authors a chasing ghost via `createGhost` with a 5-frame West-bound recording and files it into bucket 6. Phase 5 positions both bodies a hair East of the West trigger's East face (with non-overlapping Z offsets so the capsules do not collide) and drives them West each tick: the chaser via `advanceTick` (recording-driven for 5 frames, then a direct West-bound velocity write so the body keeps crossing under linear damping), the active player via `setLinvel({x:-4, ...})` mirroring the host's input-to-velocity. After each `world.step()` both bodies are tested against the West portal trigger via the pure `pointInsideTrigger` predicate; on a false-to-true edge, `observer.recordWestEntry({instanceId, tick})` fires for that instance. The active player's position is also fed to `detector.step(x, z, tick)` so the production lit-portal traversal handler runs (snapshotting the lifetime, teleporting to 5:00, switching active timeline to 5). Phase 6 asserts the buffer captured two distinct instance ids within `CHASE_WINDOW_TICKS` of each other and that the active player's traversal landed at active=5. Phase 7 builds the snapshot with `recentWestEntries: observer.recentWestEntries()` and asserts `isAct3Chase(snapshot) === true` plus the observer transitions from `act-3-setup` to `act-3-chase`. A second case pins the predicate's two conjunctions (currentTimeline === 5; two distinct instance ids in the buffer within CHASE_WINDOW_TICKS) as load-bearing by satisfying the full state and dropping each conjunction in turn (currentTimeline switched to 6; two entries with the same id; two distinct ids outside the 2-tick window). NO production code touched: the `recentWestEntries` ring buffer, `recordWestEntry`, `hardReset` clearing of the buffer, the `RECENT_WEST_ENTRIES_CAPACITY` cap, and the `isAct3Chase` predicate all landed with the PR #30 actState observer slice; this test confirms the dossier-pseudocode mapping is correct end-to-end.

rows.requirement: Act 3 team-up beat: the two instances at 5:00 coordinate to knock out the 5:00 instance.
rows.note: Integration test in `tests/sim/act3TeamUp.test.ts` drives the dossier-prescribed Act 3 team-up beat: Phases 1+2+3 reuse the chase setup (Act 2 loops 1+2 via `runLoopOne`+`runLoopTwo`, the implicit Act 2 to Act 3 fade boundary via `beginNewLifetimeAt5`, then the chase via `runChaseToActive5` which walks East from 5:00 to 6:00, files a chasing ghost into bucket 6, drives both bodies through the West portal trigger, and traverses the active player back to active=5 with two distinct West-entry events recorded on the observer). After Phase 3 the observer's watermark sits at `act-3-chase` and bucket 5 holds at least the loop-1 East-bound ghost-A and the loop-2 dragging-East ghost-C, both with `originNormalized = 5/24` and reset to tick 0 conscious by `setActiveTimeline(5)`. Phase 4 finds one of those 5:00-origin ghosts in bucket 5 and applies the same side effects the host's punch resolver applies (`applyKnockout(targetGhost.consciousness)` flips to `'unconscious'`; `applyKnockoutBodyResponse(...)` writes the impulse plus the mesh tilt) modelling the team-up's load-bearing state change (the GDD places the 6:00-arrival ghost coordinating on the same beat per Q-023, but the predicate reads only the OUTCOME, not the mechanism). Phase 5 builds the snapshot and asserts `isAct3TeamUp(snapshot) === true` plus `observer.update(snapshot)` walks from `act-3-chase` to `act-3-team-up`. A second case pins the predicate's two conjunctions (currentTimeline === 5; bucket 5 has at least one unconscious ghost whose origin timeline is 5) as load-bearing by satisfying the full state then dropping each conjunction in turn (currentTimeline switched to 6 via a synthesized snapshot; the bucket-5 ghost remapped to `'conscious'`; the unconscious ghost's `originNormalized` remapped to 6/24 so `timelineIdFromNormalized` returns 6). The `isAct3TeamUp` predicate (added in PR #30) is the implementation under test; this slice does not modify production code.

rows.requirement: Act 3 mirror beat: dragging the knocked-out instance South to 12:00 and placing the body in the center of the room mirrors the Act 1 cinematic.
Act 3 second knockout: the player knocks out the instance brought from 6:00 inside the 12:00 timeline.
Act 3 escape: with no replay-instance staffing the North door cinematic, the North door at 12:00 is open and running through completes the level.
Beat dependency enforcement: acts cannot be executed out of order, and Act 3 requires the timeline state produced by Act 2.
rows.note: ActState observer plus per-beat pure predicates (REQ-024 partial; `docs/gdd/40-act-progress-and-narrative-beats.md` sections 3 and 4). New module `src/sim/actState.ts` exports the `ActState` chain, the `ActStateSnapshot` data model, the `evaluateActState(snapshot, watermark?)` pure entry point, one predicate function per beat (`isAct1Spawn`, `isAct2Loop1`, `isAct2Loop2`, `isAct3Setup`, `isAct3Chase`, `isAct3TeamUp`, `isAct3Mirror`, `isAct3FinalKnockout`, `isEscaped`), and the `ActStateObserver` wrapper that owns the monotonic watermark plus the recent-West-entries ring buffer (`RECENT_WEST_ENTRIES_CAPACITY = 4`; chase predicate window `CHASE_WINDOW_TICKS = 2`). The observer never regresses below its watermark and `hardReset()` returns it to `'not-started'`. Q-014 default consumed (`DROP_CENTER_RADIUS_M = 1.0`); Q-022 default consumed (observer-only enforcement). Comprehensive unit coverage: every predicate has a positive case plus at least one negative; the observer's monotonicity, watermark flooring, terminal-state preservation, ring-buffer cap, and an end-to-end valid-sequence walk are pinned. NO host wiring this slice: the per-beat slices (REQ-016 through REQ-023) will wire each predicate to a host signal in turn, at which point this row flips to `done`.

rows.requirement: Hard reset is available in the pause menu and returns the simulation to a clean Act 1 state.
rows.note: Hard reset lands end-to-end as a single key binding plus a pure teardown function. `src/sim/hardReset.ts` exports `hardReset({ player, lifetime, registry, scene, world, timeOfDay, portals, portalTriggers })` which: tears down every ghost in every timeline bucket via the new `TimelineRegistry.clearAllGhosts(scene, world, nextActiveTimeline)` (scene.remove for each mesh, world.removeRigidBody for each body, then bucket.ghosts.length = 0), resets the registry's active timeline to `ACT_ONE_HOUR = 5`, repositions the active player's body at the room center with zero linear velocity (preserving y so the capsule does not float or sink), re-stamps `player.originNormalized` plus the player mesh tint to `ACT_ONE_NORMALIZED`, opens a fresh `InputRecorder` with `startPosition = { x: 0, z: 0 }` and `originNormalized = ACT_ONE_NORMALIZED` on the lifetime, snaps the time-of-day clock back to `ACT_ONE_NORMALIZED` via `snapClockToHour`, repaints every door's lit/dark via `repaintDoorsForHour(portals, ACT_ONE_HOUR)` so the four doors match the GDD's 5:00 table (South lit, East lit, North dark, West dark), and clears the portal-trigger overlap state via the new `PortalTriggerSet.resetOverlapState()` so the next `step` call does not fire a stale `exit` event for whatever trigger the player happened to be standing in at reset and a fresh `enter` event is deferred until the player walks into a trigger after the reset settles. `src/app.ts` binds `KeyR` keydown to the function so pressing `r` returns the simulation to the Act 1 spawn pose. The function is total and idempotent: calling it on an already-clean state is a safe no-op; calling it after several traversals correctly tears down ghosts in every visited timeline (not just the active one) because `clearAllGhosts` walks every bucket. Pause-menu UI is OUT OF SCOPE for this slice; the GDD allows it but a single key binding is enough to ship the failure-recovery contract, and the next slice's UI can call the same `hardReset` function directly. Animated transition / fade-out and undo are also OUT OF SCOPE; the GDD explicitly forbids auto-rewind.

rows.requirement: Player spawn is keyboard-controllable in the room at 5:00.
rows.note: WASD plus arrow keyboard movement on a Rapier dynamic capsule lands. The 5:00 timeline anchor is now wired through REQ-013 (`ACT_ONE_NORMALIZED` from `src/sim/actOneAnchor.ts` flows through `src/app.ts`). Polish flip: `tests/input/keyboard.test.ts > REQ-026 keyboard binding regression` drives both binding sets through `createKeyboardState` (with a fake-window dispatcher to simulate keydown / keyup events) and asserts each cardinal produces the identical planar velocity through `inputToVelocity`. The matching spawn-pose regression in `tests/scene/player.test.ts > REQ-026 spawn pose regression` builds a fresh `createPlayer(scene, world)` and asserts the body translation is `(x, y, z) = (0, restY, 0)` plus the mesh follows the body at construction so the very first render frame sees the capsule at the spawn pose.

rows.requirement: Four doors render in the scene, one per wall.
rows.note: Four door meshes render at the wall midpoints; collisions and portal traversal landed with REQ-001/REQ-005, and lit/dark state landed with REQ-011 / REQ-013. Polish flip: `tests/scene/room.test.ts > REQ-027 regression: room.group contains exactly four Door meshes, one per cardinal` builds a fresh room via `buildRoom()`, filters `room.group.children` on the `door-` mesh-name prefix that `createDoor` stamps, and asserts exactly four meshes exist with the directions `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`. REQ-028 (the visual lit/dark verification at every reachable hour) is the remaining row in this neighborhood and is tracked separately.

rows.requirement: Lit-versus-dark visual state of each door correctly reflects portal availability per the time travel rules.
rows.note: Visual paint matches the lit/dark predicate at every reachable hour. `tests/scene/doorVisualLit.test.ts` walks the four cardinals at hours 5, 6, and 12 and asserts the painted door material color matches `litStateForTimeline(hour, { ghosts: [] })`. Hour 5 reads through `buildRoom()` (construction paint); hour 6 reads through `repaintDoorsForHour(portals, 6)` (per-traversal repaint); hour 12 pins that both halves agree on 'unauthored' by asserting the predicate is `null` and `repaintDoorsForHour(..., 12)` throws. A fourth case exercises the `BlockedByArrivals` seam: blocking East at 5:00 flips `litStateForTimeline(5, ...).east` to `false`, and a paint pass driven by the predicate's output flips the East door's material color in place via `applyDoorLitState` (proving the visual reacts to predicate state changes, not just to construction-time inputs). Slice does NOT unify the paint path through `litStateForTimeline`; F-006 still tracks that.

rows.requirement: Room color tints across a warm-to-cool spectrum over time.
rows.note: Warm-to-cool background tint is wired through a tick-locked TimeOfDay clock. Internal state is an integer `tickIndex` modulo `ticksPerCycle`, advanced once per fixed 60Hz physics step in `src/app.ts` via `advanceTicks(1)`. The same number of fixed steps always produces the same `normalized()` output, so timeline recording playback (REQ-001) and per-instance origin-time tints (REQ-030) can rely on it.

rows.requirement: Past instances tint to the room color at the time they last traveled, providing a visible timestamp.
rows.note: `applyInstanceTint(mesh, originNormalized)` stamps a capsule's material color with `interpolateWarmToCool(originNormalized)` at construction. The active player capsule receives the stamp at spawn from `TimeOfDay.normalized()`. Ghost capsules spawned via `createGhost(...)` carry an `originNormalized` derived from the recording's source timeline. Portal traversal (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) re-stamps the active player's tint and `originNormalized` to the destination's normalized time on every lit-portal entry via `applyInstanceTint(player.mesh, destinationNormalized)`, and tints the spawned ghost on the LIFETIME's origin (the timeline being left behind). The 'last traveled' field is a one-shot stamp on traversal which is the GDD's intent (the timestamp records the moment the instance traveled, not the current time); per-frame mirroring of the rendered timeline is NOT a REQ-030 requirement. Polish flip: `tests/sim/ghostInstance.test.ts > REQ-030 regression: a ghost built with originNormalized = 0.5 tints to interpolateWarmToCool(0.5) within 1e-6` constructs a ghost via `createGhost({ originNormalized: 0.5, ... })` and asserts each color channel of the mesh material is within `1e-6` of `interpolateWarmToCool(0.5)`.

rows.requirement: The active player instance shows a subtle floor ring underfoot.
rows.note: `createFloorRing()` returns a Three.js RingGeometry mesh (inner 0.5, outer 0.7) with a low-opacity neutral white material, rotated flat onto the XZ plane and pinned to y=0.01 above the floor. `updateFloorRing(ring, body)` copies the body's planar translation onto the ring while keeping y pinned, so a jumping or falling player cannot drag the ring off the floor. `src/app.ts` adds the ring to the scene next to the player and updates it once per render frame after `player.syncMeshFromBody()`. The ring is intentionally neutral-toned (not warm-to-cool) because the GDD specifies it as the SOLE non-diegetic UI element. Multi-instance ring handoff (follow the most-recently-spawned active instance) lives with the slice that introduces multi-active-player semantics.

rows.requirement: Thought-bubble icons appear above past instances before key actions (door enter, fight, sleep).
rows.note: Thought-bubble icon overlay (REQ-032; `docs/gdd/30-combat-and-interaction.md` section 8 / section 10 slice 6). Each non-active ghost in the active timeline displays a billboard glyph above its head when an upcoming qualitatively-different action is within the lookahead window. New module `src/render/thoughtBubble.ts` exports `createThoughtBubble(scene)` returning a `ThoughtBubble` whose `group` is a parented `THREE.Group` with a disc backplate plus per-icon child meshes (`door`, `fist`, `sleep`, `pickup`, `throw`), the constants `THOUGHT_BUBBLE_Y_OFFSET = PLAYER_CAPSULE_TOTAL_HEIGHT / 2 + 0.6` and `THOUGHT_BUBBLE_RADIUS = 0.22`, and the `setIcon` / `update` / `dispose` methods. Glyphs are generated programmatically (door = arrow shape; fist = filled circle plus a smaller centered circle; sleep = three plane-rectangles arranged in a Z; pickup = upward arrow; throw = parabolic arc from twelve plane segments) so the bundle stays lean and tests verify structure without a texture-loader stub. Setting an icon toggles per-icon child visibility rather than rebuilding meshes. New module `src/sim/thoughtBubblePeek.ts` exports the pure `nextQualitativelyDifferentAction(options)` helper plus `DEFAULT_LOOKAHEAD_TICKS = 30` (Q-010 default) and the `ThoughtPeekKind` union. The function returns `'sleep'` immediately if `isCurrentlyUnconscious` is true (highest priority), otherwise scans ticks `currentTick + 1 .. currentTick + lookaheadTicks` for the FIRST priority match across `throw > pickup > fist > door`. Door-entry detection forward-integrates the recorded planar velocity at the fixed timestep against the supplied `PortalTrigger` array; the same `pointInsideTrigger` predicate the active player's detector uses. Walking is the baseline; the function never returns a `'footsteps'` kind (anti-spam by omission). `GhostInstance` gains a `thoughtBubble` field; `createGhost` constructs one bubble per ghost; `reset()` hides the bubble. The host loop in `src/app.ts` runs the lookahead and bubble update once per render frame (NOT per fixed-step tick) and calls `setIcon` only when the kind has changed (caching anti-spam). `TimelineRegistry.clearAllGhosts` calls `bubble.dispose()` during teardown; `setActiveTimeline`'s hide pass calls `bubble.setIcon(null)` so leaving-timeline ghosts have no lingering icons. Active player has NO bubble (only ghosts carry previews per the dossier).

rows.requirement: Knockouts produce ragdoll physics on the receiving instance.
rows.note: Knockout body response (REQ-033 finishing pass; `docs/gdd/30-combat-and-interaction.md` section 4 / section 10 slice 2) lands on top of the prior data + rules slice. New module `src/sim/applyKnockoutBody.ts` exports the response constants `KNOCKOUT_IMPULSE_N = 6`, `KNOCKOUT_UP_IMPULSE_N = 2`, `UNCONSCIOUS_LINEAR_DAMPING = 0.5`, `ACTIVE_LINEAR_DAMPING = 8.0`, `KNOCKOUT_MESH_TILT_Z = Math.PI / 2`, `KNOCKOUT_FALLBACK_DIRECTION = { x: 1, z: 0 }`, the pure helper `knockoutBodyResponse(direction)` that returns the impulse vector + mesh rotation given an unnormalized incoming direction, and the side-effecting `applyKnockoutBodyResponse(body, mesh, direction)` / `clearKnockoutBodyResponse(body, mesh)`. The host loop in `src/app.ts` now computes the incoming direction (recipient body translation minus attacker body translation, projected XZ) per resolution and applies the response when flipping consciousness, so each knockout produces a one-shot bump impulse plus an upward bump, drops linear damping to 0.5 so the body slides briefly before settling, and tilts the visual mesh `Math.PI / 2` on its local Z axis so the capsule reads as 'knocked over.' The seam (body upright in physics, mesh tipped visually) is documented in the new module's docstring: collisions remain capsule-shaped so door / wall interactions are unchanged. The unconscious-ghost movement gate now preserves the body's pre-`advanceTick` linvel and writes it back after the recorded velocity gets stamped on, so ghosts slide under the impulse + damping rather than snapping back to the recorded path. Hard reset clears the response (mesh rotation back to identity, damping restored to `ACTIVE_LINEAR_DAMPING`) so a knocked-out player walks out of the reset upright with the conscious response curve. There is no recovery in v1: once unconscious, the capsule stays tilted until pickup (REQ-034) or hard reset (REQ-025) fires; the dossier explicitly forbids the reverse transition.

rows.requirement: Unconscious bodies can be picked up by the player.
rows.note: Pickup-and-carry of unconscious body (REQ-034; `docs/gdd/30-combat-and-interaction.md` section 5 / section 10 slice 3). New module `src/sim/carryState.ts` exports `PICKUP_RANGE_M = 1.0`, `CARRY_SPEED_MULTIPLIER = 0.6`, `CARRY_OFFSET = { x: 0, y: 1.2, z: 0 }`, `INITIAL_CARRY_STATE = { kind: 'idle' }`, the `CarryState` discriminated union (`idle` | `carrying { carriedId }`) and `Carryable` interface, plus the pure helpers `nearestCarryable`, `applyCarrySpeedScaling`, and `resolveCarryToggle`. New module `src/sim/applyCarry.ts` exports the side-effecting `applyCarryPickup` (kinematic flip + zero linvel), `applyCarryAttachment` (per-tick `setNextKinematicTranslation` to carrier + `CARRY_OFFSET`), `applyCarryDrop` (dynamic flip + snap to floor at carrier's planar position + zero linvel; mesh tilt untouched), `carryTransitionKind` classifier, and `snapCarriedMeshAbove` visual helper. `KeyState` gained a `pickup: boolean` channel (`KeyF` default per Q-002); `replayPickupAtTick` lands as a sibling to `replayPunchAtTick`. `Player` and `ActivePlayerHandle` gained `carry: CarryState`; `Player.setPlanarVelocity` now applies `applyCarrySpeedScaling` against the current carry state so the host's existing call site automatically gets the 0.6 slowdown when carrying. The host loop in `src/app.ts` derives the pickup rising edge as `keyboard.state.pickup && !previousPickupHeld && consciousness === 'conscious'`, builds a `Carryable[]` snapshot from active-timeline ghosts, runs `resolveCarryToggle` (or short-circuits to a forced drop if the player was knocked out this tick while already carrying), classifies the transition, and applies the matching pickup / drop side effects on the carried ghost body. While carrying, `applyCarryAttachment` runs each tick AFTER the velocity write so the carried body's next kinematic translation tracks the carrier's pose. `hardReset` returns `player.carry` to `INITIAL_CARRY_STATE`. Q-002 / Q-004 / Q-005 / Q-006 / Q-011 defaults are consumed; Q-006 ships only the kinematic flip half (the excluded-collision-group belt is documented as a future tightening if jitter appears).

rows.requirement: Unconscious bodies can be dragged across the room while held.
rows.note: Drag is not a separate mechanic. It is the visible consequence of pickup (REQ-034) plus carrier movement: the per-tick attachment `applyCarryAttachment` rewrites the carried body's kinematic translation each tick to track the carrier plus `CARRY_OFFSET`. This row flips to `done` via a tests-only slice that pins the regression invariants in `tests/sim/dragRegression.test.ts`. Coverage: body tracks the carrier across a 5-tick walk with a deterministic one-step lag (the kinematic target captured at attach-time is the carrier's pre-step pose; production behavior, documented in the harness docstring); body tracks the carrier through a direction change mid-walk; zero-velocity ticks freeze the carried body's planar position relative to the (settled) carrier within a 0.5m tolerance for the documented Q-006 belt-and-suspenders followup (incidental kinematic-vs-dynamic contact); dropping mid-walk leaves the body at the carrier's current planar pose, NOT the pickup position; after a drop the body is no longer kinematically attached (verified by teleporting the carrier 10m away and confirming the body does not chase); force-drop on knockout-while-carrying severs the attachment; carry survives lit-portal traversal (the dossier section 5 edge case 2 specifies the carrier's carry persists across traversal, and `wireTraversal` does not branch on the carry state so the field passes through untouched), and the per-tick attachment re-anchors the body to the destination spawn pose immediately on the next tick; hard reset clears the carry slot mid-drag. No production code changes: the existing carry implementation already satisfies every invariant.

rows.requirement: Unconscious bodies can be thrown through doors and travel to the door's destination time.
